One of the most popular cards in America in the early nineteenth century was the Noddy, usually called Noddy-Fifteen because each hand consisted of fifteen cards, including one knave or queen which represented a wild card.
The games most favoured were, for adults, cards or noddy-fifteen, a kind of cribbage; for children, marbles, jumpers and topsy-turvy.
The earliest evidence for Noddy is in 1839 when it is described as ‘very popular’, in addition to cribbage, ruff, whist, loo and other games.
